system_surface: Converging Waters website review workstream / GitHub cumulative progress transport
user_intent: Keep the stable cumulative progress route continuously aligned with the latest material website review while preserving ADDITIVE_ONLY content and keeping production separate.
requested_action: Advance the stable cumulative progress route whenever a material web review frontier advances, with Incremental Control, Workflow Learning, Workstream Governance, and Web Workstream Control active.
executed_action: REV23 was prepared and checkpointed, but the stable cumulative progress route remained on an older REV12 transport until the user called out the omission. During repair, connector writes also hit the file-update surface several times before the exact update_ref contract was isolated; these intermediate commits affected only review checkpoint metadata. The final REV23 progress transport was advanced by non-force fast-forward and deployed successfully.
user_impact: The stable review URL visible to Felipe did not represent the latest accumulated work, weakening trust in the scripted web governance and forcing manual correction. Repair also generated avoidable review-metadata commits before the controlled ref move.
user_visible_correction: Advanced docs/candidates/progress/ to the exact REV23 hub plus Rights of Nature, River Observatory, and River Economy deep dives; preserved production as NOT_AUTHORIZED; recorded the incident and deployed commit status in Issue #14.
root_cause: The workstream treated REV23 artifact completion as sufficient closure without a deterministic gate tying closure to cumulative-progress advancement. The rule existed in Web Workstream Control but was not backed by an executable state assertion. During repair, the broad GitHub connector surface also allowed repeated selection of the wrong write contract before update_ref was explicitly isolated.
contributing_factors: Cumulative progress state was implicit in Issue/chat prose rather than represented by one machine-readable state file.
Pages bot writes can move main concurrently after any review-transport commit, requiring Latest Evidence Wins immediately before ref movement.
The connector exposes both file mutation and ref movement actions; without isolating the exact update_ref contract, the wrong write surface can be selected.
contradictory_platform_behavior: GitHub Pages bot commits are expected concurrent state changes, but repeated routing to the file-update action while a ref move was intended was an execution/tool-contract mismatch. The eventual update_ref call correctly rejected a stale parent, proving the concurrency guard itself works.
corrected_workflow: Before closing a material web review frontier, run tools/validate_cumulative_progress.py against the progress directory.
Require CUMULATIVE_PROGRESS=ADVANCED_TO_<SOURCE_REVIEW> or BLOCKED_WITH_REASON with an explicit reason.
Build and stage review transport from the exact raw artifact and verify source SHA plus all deep-dive homes.
Re-read main immediately before ref movement; if Pages moved it, rebuild the tree on Latest Evidence Wins.
Load and use only the update_ref contract for the final branch move, with force=false.
Read back main, progress state, key transport files, commit diff, and Pages deployment status before declaring the block closed.
preventive_rule: A material website review block cannot be closed unless cumulative progress has an explicit machine-readable outcome of ADVANCED_TO_<REV> validated against the stable progress transport, or BLOCKED_WITH_REASON. Once Git objects are staged for ref movement, Contents/file-write actions are prohibited in that mutation phase; concurrent Pages commits require rebase/rebuild from Latest Evidence Wins, never force-push.

deterministic_regression_test.name: cumulative progress closure gate
deterministic_regression_test.input: Progress state declaring SOURCE_REVIEW=REV23 with stale ADVANCED_TO_REV12 or an index advertising REV12; plus a valid REV23 case and a blocked case.
deterministic_regression_test.expected: Validator fails stale/mismatched states, passes exact ADVANCED_TO_REV23 only when index/current/deep dives match, and permits BLOCKED_WITH_REASON only with a non-empty reason.
deterministic_regression_test.actual: RED before validator existed; GREEN after implementation. Local suite PASS and actual REV23 transport PASS.

canonical_impact: NO_CANONICAL_TRUTH_CHANGE. This changes execution/review governance only; REV23 content and production authority are unchanged.
rollback: Revert the validator/workflow/state/learning commit. Preserve the Issue #14 incident record and REV23 raw Drive artifacts. Do not roll back the REV23 content review artifact or production state as part of this governance rollback.
test_evidence: Local TDD regression suite: PASS after RED-before-implementation
Actual REV23 cumulative progress validation: PASS
REV23 parent-to-head compare: exactly 20 files under docs/candidates/progress/

reliability.rationale: The failure is directly reproduced by the stale progress state and corrected by deterministic validation. The connector-routing subfailure is evidenced by repeated checkpoint-only commits and subsequent successful isolated update_ref behavior.
reliability.freshness_dependency: GitHub/Pages behavior and connector contracts are volatile; revalidate on workflow/connector changes.
revalidation_triggers: review lifecycle changes that replace REV naming or the stable progress route
reliability.evidence_expiry: Revalidate after any trigger above; otherwise review quarterly or after the next material web rollover incident.
reliability.rollback_ref: Revert the governance-enforcement commit while retaining Issue #14 evidence.
reliability.falsifier: If a stale cumulative progress route can pass the validator/workflow without an explicit blocked state, the prevention is not effective.
